outcomes.name: Theme and central idea
outcomes.description: Finds what a text is really about and traces how it develops.

outcomes.name: Point of view and purpose
outcomes.description: Explains how an author’s perspective and purpose shape a text.

outcomes.name: Development
outcomes.description: Tracks how ideas, characters, or events build across a text.

outcomes.name: Structure
outcomes.description: Explains how the parts of a text fit together and why.

outcomes.name: Word choice
outcomes.description: Explains how specific words and phrases shape meaning and tone.

outcomes.name: Selecting relevant sources
outcomes.description: Chooses sources that fit the question and says why.

outcomes.name: Contextualizing sources
outcomes.description: Places a source in its time, place, and purpose.

outcomes.name: Synthesizing multiple sources
outcomes.description: Brings several sources together into one line of thinking.

outcomes.name: Asking questions
outcomes.description: Writes questions that can be investigated and matter.

outcomes.name: Hypothesizing
outcomes.description: Proposes a testable explanation grounded in what is known.

outcomes.name: Designing processes and procedures
outcomes.description: Plans a fair method with the right variables and controls.

outcomes.name: Collecting data
outcomes.description: Gathers accurate, organized data the method calls for.

outcomes.name: Making connections and inferences
outcomes.description: Reads between the lines and links ideas across contexts.

outcomes.name: Critiquing the reasoning of others
outcomes.description: Finds the strengths and gaps in someone else’s argument.

outcomes.name: Justifying and constructing an explanation
outcomes.description: Builds an explanation that follows from the evidence.

outcomes.name: Interpreting data and information
outcomes.description: Says what the data shows and what it does not.

outcomes.name: Modeling
outcomes.description: Represents a system or situation so it can be reasoned about.

outcomes.name: Comparing and contrasting
outcomes.description: Weighs similarities and differences to reach a point.

outcomes.name: Argumentative claim
outcomes.description: States a clear, defensible position.

outcomes.name: Informational and explanatory thesis
outcomes.description: Frames a focused, informative thesis.

outcomes.name: Narrative
outcomes.description: Tells a story with purpose, pacing, and detail.

outcomes.name: Counterclaims
outcomes.description: Takes opposing views seriously and answers them.

outcomes.name: Selection of evidence
outcomes.description: Picks the evidence that best supports the point.

outcomes.name: Explanation of evidence
outcomes.description: Says how the evidence proves the point.

outcomes.name: Integration of evidence
outcomes.description: Weaves evidence into the writing so it reads as one piece.

outcomes.name: Organization
outcomes.description: Orders ideas so the reader can follow, with transitions that carry the logic.

outcomes.name: Introduction and conclusion
outcomes.description: Opens with purpose and closes with meaning.

outcomes.name: Discussion and contribution
outcomes.description: Moves a conversation forward with ideas that build on others.

outcomes.name: Preparation
outcomes.description: Comes ready with the reading done and a stance to test.

outcomes.name: Norms and active listening
outcomes.description: Listens to understand and keeps the group’s agreements.

outcomes.name: Style and language
outcomes.description: Matches tone and word choice to audience and purpose.

outcomes.name: Oral presentation
outcomes.description: Presents clearly with voice, pacing, and presence.

outcomes.name: Multimedia in written production
outcomes.description: Uses visuals and media to strengthen written work.

outcomes.name: Multimedia in oral presentation
outcomes.description: Uses media to support, never replace, the spoken message.

outcomes.name: Conventions
outcomes.description: Uses grammar, usage, and mechanics that help the reader.

outcomes.name: Precision
outcomes.description: Says exactly what is meant with the right level of detail.

outcomes.name: Attachment
outcomes.description: Has at least one adult at school who knows me well.

outcomes.name: Stress management
outcomes.description: Notices stress and has ways to steady myself.

outcomes.name: Self-regulation
outcomes.description: Manages attention, feelings, and actions toward a goal.

outcomes.name: Self-awareness
outcomes.description: Knows my strengths, values, and what I need to learn well.

outcomes.name: Social awareness and relationship skills
outcomes.description: Reads others well and builds relationships that work.

outcomes.name: Executive function
outcomes.description: Plans, organizes, and follows through on multi-step work.

outcomes.name: Growth mindset
outcomes.description: Believes ability grows with effort and good strategies.

outcomes.name: Self-efficacy
outcomes.description: Believes I can do hard things and shows it.

outcomes.name: Sense of belonging
outcomes.description: Feels part of this school and this community.

outcomes.name: Relevance of school
outcomes.description: Connects the work at school to the life I am building.

outcomes.name: Resilience
outcomes.description: Comes back from setbacks and keeps going.

outcomes.name: Agency
outcomes.description: Acts on my own choices and takes ownership of the outcome.

outcomes.name: Academic tenacity
outcomes.description: Sticks with challenging work until it is done well.

outcomes.name: Self-direction
outcomes.description: Sets goals, chooses strategies, and checks my own progress.

outcomes.name: Curiosity
outcomes.description: Asks questions and follows them where they lead.

outcomes.name: Civic identity
outcomes.description: Sees myself as someone who contributes to a community.

outcomes.name: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed...
outcomes.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

outcomes.name: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on...
outcomes.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

outcomes.name: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros t...
outcomes.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

outcomes.name: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships
outcomes.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. *For example, the polynomial identity (x^2 + y^2)^2 = (x^2, y^2)^2 + (2xy)^2 can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.*

outcomes.name: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(...
outcomes.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

outcomes.name: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems
outcomes.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

outcomes.name: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; grap...
outcomes.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

outcomes.name: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequa...
outcomes.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. *For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.*

outcomes.name: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solvin...
outcomes.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. *For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.*

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asse...
outcomes.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities

outcomes.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities

outcomes.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.
outcomes.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

outcomes.name: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equa...
outcomes.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)^2 = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2 = 49), taking square roots, completing...
outcomes.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the s...
outcomes.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on...
outcomes.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plo...
outcomes.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y...
outcomes.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

outcomes.domain: Algebra: reasoning with equations and inequalities
outcomes.name: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the bo...
outcomes.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

outcomes.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. *For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.*

outcomes.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

outcomes.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

outcomes.name: Find inverse functions.
outcomes.description: Find inverse functions.

outcomes.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. *For example, f(x) = 2x^3 or f(x) = (x+1)/(x, 1) for x  1.*

outcomes.name: Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationshi...
outcomes.description: (+) Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

outcomes.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

outcomes.name: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statemen...
outcomes.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

outcomes.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. *For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n  1.*

outcomes.name: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of g...
outcomes.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.

outcomes.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. *For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.*

outcomes.name: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graph...
outcomes.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). *For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.*
